_what: THE BATTERY A FAMILY ACTUALLY BRINGS — the denominator for any change to retrieval or the relevance floor.
_why: Four candidate sharpenings of ask._title_names_subject were measured on 2026-11-21 and all four
died: a subject-ratio floor was ALGEBRAICALLY the current rule (real subjects are 1-2 stems);
len>=2 cost 95% of true answers; a reference-shelf gate capped at 34% of collisions and could not
be fitted without fitting to its own battery; and a body-evidence floor recovered almost none of
the prize because it demands the asker's literal words. 98.54% of relevant evidence is invisible
None of that could be graded properly, and THAT is the finding this file answers. The repo's
query->right-answer labels total: 22 (eval/word_questions.json, shelf labels), 8 (lead.id in
eval/live_probes.jsonl), 12 (keyword expectations in eval/coherent_model), 12 (synonym groups in
tools/retrieval_assay.py GOLDEN). That scarcity is why a reweighting can always be made to look
good: a zero without its denominator is uninterpretable, and so is a win.
WRITTEN BEFORE ANY RULE WAS BUILT, deliberately, so it cannot be fitted to the rule it grades.
The questions come from what a household asks and the labels from the shelf inventory alone
(130 shelves / 935,267 cards, counted 2026-11-21). NO SEARCH WAS RUN TO CHOOSE A LABEL, and no
candidate rule was consulted. A golden set built by running the search and blessing what came
back scores 1.000 forever and measures nothing (tools/retrieval_assay.py says this in its own
words); so does one written after seeing a rule's misses.
_the_rule_this_file_imposes_on_its_reade: READING THIS FILE'S FAILURES IN ORDER TO DESIGN A FIX BURNS IT. eval/word_questions.json was
burned exactly that way on 2026-11-21: its 13 detector misses were read, so the word-intent
triggers can no longer be graded on it. If you design against these questions, write the next
sibling before you build, the way this one was.
Grade the WHOLE file every time. Reporting only the questions a change improves is the same
self-confirming metric in a new coat.

_how_to_grade.expect shelf_in: PASS when the LEADING source sits on one of the named shelves. Any of them is right.
_how_to_grade.MISRETRIEVAL: A leader on an unnamed shelf. This is the defect the floor exists to prevent, and it is the number that matters: a confident irrelevant hit is worse than silence.
_how_to_grade.GAP: An honest miss. NOT a defect — it is a want. Several shelves a family needs are nearly empty (survival 24 cards, sanitation 24, fieldkit 30, practical 3,058, against dictionary 149,490 and pronunciation 125,167), so a large gap count here is a statement about the keeping, not about retrieval.
_how_to_grade.expect crisis: PASS only when help comes first and retrieval never runs. Any card served here is a FAILURE however apt.
_how_to_grade.expect miss: PASS only on an honest miss. Serving anything is a fabrication.
_how_to_grade.report: three counts per run — PASS / MISRETRIEVAL / GAP — never a single score, because a floor can always trade one for another.

_kinds.howto: plainly phrased as a task; the lane the engine was built for
_kinds.situation: a person describing what is happening, with no 'how do I'. The gate wants a how-to and a parent describes a situation (2026-11-20), so these are the ones that fall through
_kinds.synonym: phrased in words the keeping probably does not use literally ('put up beans' for canning), to test vocabulary bridging rather than literal overlap
_kinds.collision: contains a word that collides hard with a reference shelf; the right answer is still the practical one
_kinds.out_of_corpus: no honest answer exists; the only pass is a miss

_correction_2026_11_21: The first labels were written from a shelf listing truncated at the top 70 of 130, so every small
domain shelf was invisible and 'how do I stop a wound from bleeding' was scored MISRETRIEVAL for a
correct first_aid lead. Relabelled against the full live box inventory (127 shelves) by a topic->shelf
map applied UNIFORMLY to all rows, adding shelves only, never removing. A truncated listing reads
exactly like an absence -- the same error as a paginated API listing earlier the same day.
NOTE for anyone grading a rule on this file: the shelf labels are now GENEROUS. A generous label makes
MISRETRIEVAL harder to score, so that count is a LOWER bound on the defect, and PASS stays an upper
bound. Both directions are stated so neither can be read as better than it is.
